CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up in HIV-positive patient.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy. Patient reports feeling well on current regimen with improved vigor and sleep quality. Notes positive effects on bloodwork. Currently on testosterone 1 mL every 10 days at 140 mg dose. Patient reports compliance with medications and is taking correct steps to improve his life. Denies weight loss but notes improved sense of well-being. Patient inquired about increasing testosterone dose to 175 mg but was counseled against this due to risk of elevated peak levels exceeding 1,500 ng/dL, which increases risk of polycythemia and cardiovascular complications. Patient was advised to maintain current dose.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports good energy levels and improved sleep. Denies physical changes despite subjective well-being. No acute complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV infection
Hypogonadism
History of elevated triglycerides (now improved)

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone injection 1 mL every 10 days (140 mg dose)
Finasteride 2.5 mg daily (patient taking half of 5 mg tablet)
Cialis 2.5-5 mg daily (5 mg on workout days)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient uses Walmart pharmacy for medications. Prefers paper prescriptions. Uses medication calendar to track testosterone injections. Patient on day 8 of current testosterone cycle, due for next injection Thursday or Friday.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing male, trim appearance
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no concerns
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no concerns
No acute distress noted

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (prior 0.5 ng/mL, stable)
Testosterone: Last level >1,500 ng/dL (drawn shortly after injection)
Cholesterol: Improved significantly
Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (improved from prior 265 mg/dL)
Red blood cell count: Increased but stable
Estradiol: Not elevated

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Hypogonadism on testosterone replacement: Continue current dose of testosterone 1 mL (140 mg) every 10 days. Discussed risks of dose escalation including potential for polycythemia and cardiovascular complications given peak testosterone levels >1,500 ng/dL. Patient counseled against increasing to 175 mg at this time. Patient remains stable and compliant with excellent subjective response.
2. Finasteride: Continue 2.5 mg daily.
3. Cialis: Continue 2.5-5 mg daily as needed.
4. PSA: Stable, continue annual monitoring.
5. Estradiol: No current elevation; may retest in fall if patient desires.
6. Prescriptions: Renew testosterone, finasteride, and cialis with paper prescriptions as requested.
